quotes.text: Grasp a dumbbell in each hand, and stand with your feet close to shoulder-width apart.
quotes.closest: Grasp a dumbbell in each hand, and stand with your feet close to shoulder-width apart.

quotes.text: Position each dumbbell in front of you with your palms facing your body.
quotes.closest: Position each dumbbell in front of you with your palms facing your body.

quotes.text: Raise one dumbbell in an arc toward your opposite shoulder by engaging the bicep of that arm.
quotes.closest: Raise one dumbbell in an arc toward your opposite shoulder by engaging the bicep of that arm.

quotes.text: Lock your elbow in place for the duration of the exercise.
quotes.closest: Lock your elbow in place for the duration of the exercise.

quotes.text: Hold the dumbbell in position at the top of this movement for a moment.
quotes.closest: Hold the dumbbell in position at the top of this movement for a moment.

quotes.text: Maintain tension in your bicep as you bring the dumbbell back to its starting position by reversing the movement.

quotes.text: Unlike many other Hammer Curl variations, this exercises has you bring the weight across your body instead of straight up and down.
quotes.closest: Unlike many other Hammer Curl variations, this exercises has you bring the weight across your body instead of straight up and down.

quotes.text: Using momentum, or recruiting additional muscle groups can help you lift heavier weights with this exercise. However it also reduces the effectiveness, and increases the risk of injury. Keep your weights on the lighter side, and focus on controlling the weight.
quotes.closest: Using momentum, or recruiting additional muscle groups can help you lift heavier weights with this exercise. However it also reduces the effectiveness, and increases the risk of injury. Keep your weights on the lighter side, and focus on controlling the weight.

quotes.text: Maintain a neutral wrist position (wrist straight without any bend with your palms facing your body) and avoid shrugging your shoulders throughout the movement.
quotes.closest: Maintain a neutral wrist position (wrist straight without any bend with your palms facing your body) and avoid shrugging your shoulders throughout the movement.

quotes.text: stiffen your torso by contracting your abdominal/core muscles ("bracing"), and depress and retract your scapulae (pull your shoulders down and back), maintaining these positions throughout the exercise.
